gap: Can one bounded recursive-trajectory correction to the fast SO(3) readout improve the first cold-start and early 250 ms physical forecasts without forfeiting its online speed?
roster: One fresh candidate fit per case. Reuse the authenticated previous SO(3) readout predictions as control; require exact matching fresh initial model arrays before correction. Correct the prefix once from its last completed 250 ms window, score origin zero, then observe through exactly the next previously frozen conditional origin and score every native one-step prediction before revealing truth. This is 16 post-prefix updates on each of the six older tapes, 25 on paired-quad-fine and 5 on paired-quad-coarse, 126 total. Score 50,100,150,200,250 ms at both origins. Future issued commands enter scoring only, never a correction.

algorithm.base: Unchanged physical SO(3) direct readout with fresh prefix, measured-increment G/Q, curvature, body-motion and physical-attitude penalties. No frozen fleet features, vehicle metadata, output-specific vehicle branch or changed physical integrator.
algorithm.causal_window: At the prefix and after each new observation, take exactly the most recent completed 250 ms physical trajectory: H=round(0.25/dt) issued commands and H+1 measured observations, plus the required 0.5 s preceding context. No state after the correction time is accessed. The candidate stores this bounded context itself.
algorithm.residual: At the single 250 ms endpoint compute r=[predicted world velocity minus observed world velocity in m/s, predicted body rate minus observed body rate in rad/s, (predicted rotation minus observed rotation)/sqrt(2)]. Flatten the nine rotation entries. This gives a 15-vector with geodesic-equivalent small-angle norm, in fixed physical units; no sensor-noise or vehicle-specific scale is inferred.
algorithm.linearization: Differentiate r with JAX reverse AD with respect to all P-by-6 direct readout weights at the uncorrected direct solution M, holding frozen feature/filter/memory parameters and known physics fixed. J has shape 15 by 6P. Whiten columns with c_j=1/sqrt(max(1,G_jj)), repeated across six outputs, where G is the direct readout's causal data-plus-prefix-ridge Gram. Compute a single dual ridge correction z=-(Jc).T[(Jc)(Jc).T+I_15]^-1 r, then cap ||z||_2 at 1 and set delta=c*z. This is one Gauss-Newton linearization, not a hyperparameter search.
algorithm.acceptance: Try exactly multipliers 1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 in that order on delta; accept the first finite actual 250 ms completed-window residual norm strictly below the uncorrected direct solution. Otherwise retain direct M. Recompute from direct M after every observation, not from the previous correction. No new observation is assimilated twice.
algorithm.prefix: The correction at the initial origin uses only the prefix states/commands; include all its acquisition, construction, compilation, Jacobian and solve time. Source begin:first includes the fixed-wing 0–0.75 s and quad 0.5–1.25 s prefixes, not free pretraining. The first scored prediction is made after this correction and before any post-prefix observation.

evaluation.metrics: Save and report per-case first and next-frozen-origin physical velocity, body-rate and SO(3) orientation errors at 50,100,150,200,250 ms, plus every native one-step prediction through that next origin. Compare candidate/previous direct readout and candidate/full learner in physical units; never combine 10 and 50 ms native one-step scores. Report per-family 250 ms velocity/rate flags as informative, not automatic vetoes.
evaluation.timing: Single exclusive CPU process. Time complete prefix correction, first prediction and each observe plus direct solve, trajectory Jacobian, dual solve, actual-loss backtracking and model snapshot; report first, warm median/p95, total, accepted correction count and residual decrease. Historical control times are separate-run references.
evaluation.decision: A promising screen must reduce first-origin body-rate error on both fixed-wing recordings without increasing either first-origin velocity error by over 50%, keep all forecasts finite, and avoid a major consistent 250 ms loss at the next frozen origin on the quad cases. A complete correction update slower than the current full learner is a negative runtime result, not an accuracy veto. Report all attempted and failed cases; no automatic production adoption. If prefix correction helps but repeated correction fails, isolate the prefix result before changing a strength.
evaluation.stopping: At most 25 post-prefix corrections per case, 126 candidate updates overall, one fixed design and strength, one planned attempt, 600 s wall limit. Stop on nonfinite model/forecast/Jacobian, source mismatch or time limit and preserve the attempt.

verification: Commit this protocol before implementation and complete scientific code before the first fit. Unit-check the 15-by-6P Jacobian against centered directional finite differences, the dual ridge solution against its normal equations and the trust cap, and stale/duplicate observation rejection. Authenticate every source and completed pack. Save every correction's r,J,c,dual solution, trial norms, multiplier, resulting delta and model fingerprint, along with all candidate predictions/truth/timings/initial and final models. Independently recompute scores, acceptance and dual algebra from saved arrays without fitting, and reject altered artifacts. Delete the one-off code after reporting; preserve it in committed history.
